- backup on node of aws.rds: RDS automated backups. Daily snapshots plus transaction logs enable point-in-time restore within the retention period.
- backup on node of aws.aurora: Aurora automated backups. Continuous, incremental backups to S3 enable point-in-time restore within the retention period.
- backup on node of aws.efs: EFS backups with AWS Backup. Policy-based automatic backups of a file system through AWS Backup.
- backup on node of aws.elasticache: ElastiCache snapshots. Point-in-time snapshots of a Valkey or Redis OSS cluster, restorable into a new cluster.
- backup on node of aws.s3: S3 versioning. Keeps multiple versions of each object so overwrites and deletes can be undone. Value: versioning.
- multiAz on node of aws.rds: RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Synchronous standby in another Availability Zone with automatic failover.
- multiAz on node of aws.aurora: Aurora Multi-AZ (replicas across zones). Aurora replicas in other Availability Zones provide automatic failover.
- multiAz on node of aws.elasticache: ElastiCache Multi-AZ. Replicas in other Availability Zones with automatic failover for Valkey and Redis OSS.
- replication on node of aws.s3: S3 cross-region replication. Asynchronously copies new objects to a bucket in another Region.
- replication on node of aws.dynamodb: DynamoDB global tables. Multi-Region, multi-active replication of a table.
- replication on node of aws.aurora: Aurora global database. One primary Region plus read-only secondary Regions with fast cross-Region replication.
- replication on node of aws.rds: RDS cross-region read replica. A read replica in another Region for disaster recovery and local reads.
- encryption on node of aws.s3: S3 encryption at rest. Encrypts S3 data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.dynamodb: DynamoDB encryption at rest. Encrypts DynamoDB data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.rds: RDS encryption at rest. Encrypts RDS data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.aurora: Aurora encryption at rest. Encrypts Aurora data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.efs: EFS encryption at rest. Encrypts EFS data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.elasticache: ElastiCache encryption at rest. Encrypts ElastiCache data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.sqs: SQS encryption at rest. Encrypts SQS data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.
- encryption on node of aws.sns: SNS encryption at rest. Encrypts SNS data at rest. Value: exactly "KMS" or "AWS-managed"; KMS means a customer managed key.

data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","content_index":0,"item_id":"msg_0e757ba21a8c08b2016af00adf728c87d09a658a872d4041b2","logprobs":[],"output_index":1,"sequence_number":3954,"text":"{
  "name": "Dental Clinic Booking",
  "inferredRequirements": [
    {
      "id": "I1",
      "text": "Prevent concurrent bookings for the same appointment slot and make booking and cancellation requests idempotent.",
      "type": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "I2",
      "text": "Monitor application failures and reminder delivery failures without exposing patient data in logs.",
      "type": "non-functional"
    }
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The application is a new standalone scheduling system; no existing practice-management or patient-record integration or data migration is required.",
    "Patients authenticate through Amazon Cognito using verified email addresses. Staff use administrator-provisioned accounts with mandatory MFA; patients cannot assign themselves staff roles or clinic memberships.",
    "The deployment is provisionally treated as a US HIPAA-regulated workload. Before production, the operator must confirm applicable jurisdiction, execute required agreements including an AWS BAA, and verify service and messaging-channel eligibility. Architecture alone does not establish compliance.",
    "Email and SMS contain only generic reminders and a link to sign in, without names, treatment details, clinic specialties, or appointment details. Messaging requires verified contact information and appropriate patient consent.",
    "A single AWS Region approved by the operator for patient-data residency is sufficient. Clinical records and payments are outside scope.",
    "Clinics have predefined appointment slots and configured time zones. Reminders are sent during the morning of the preceding local calendar day, rather than exactly 24 hours beforehand.",
    "An hourly reminder job is sufficient for approximately 5,000 patients. It reads date-partitioned appointment indexes and rechecks current booking status before sending.",
    "Reminder delivery uses per-appointment, per-channel delivery records and conditional claims to suppress routine duplicates. A timeout after a provider accepts a message can still produce a duplicate on retry; exactly-once external delivery is not assumed.",
    "Deployment includes least-privilege execution roles, restricted bucket policies, HTTPS-only access, log redaction and retention controls, and application authorization tests."
  ],
